name: Cancer Research Institute
mission: The Cancer Research Institute’s mission is to create a world immune to cancer by driving scientific discovery, accelerating collaboration, and turning breakthroughs into life-saving treatments.
programs: William B. Coley Award for Distinguished Research in Basic and Tumor Immunology
CRI Lloyd J. Old STAR Program
AACR-CRI Lloyd J. Old Award in Cancer Immunology
theoryOfChange: Over the next five years, the Cancer Research Institute will aim to:(a) bring increasingly effective cancer immunotherapies to more cancer patient populations;(b) expand awareness among patients, caregivers, and health care professionals of the power of cancer immunotherapy and its significant potential to slow or halt tumor growth, delay or prevent cancer recurrence, and extend patient lives, including members of underrepresented minority communities including Black, Hispanic and Latino/Latina, Asian American and Pacific Islander, and Indigenous populations;(c) grow the general public's awareness of the revolution in cancer treatment and the need to continue funding critical research in order to optimize immunotherapy for more groups of cancer patients;

strengths_deep_dive: The Cancer Research Institute maintains strong financial discipline alongside a long operational history since 1953 [2]. In FY2024, the organization spent <cite id="8">84.0% of its budget directly on programs</cite>, outperforming the 75% sector baseline [8]. Institutional health is further supported by <cite id="7">21.2 months of working capital reserves</cite> and a low fundraising expense ratio of <cite id="7">$0.11 per $1 raised</cite> [7]. Independent evaluators confirm these operational standards, yielding a <cite id="7">94/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite> [7].
rich_narrative.summary: Founded in 1953, the Cancer Research Institute (CRI) funds clinician-scientists and specialized research initiatives to advance cancer immunotherapy [2]. In FY2024, the organization reported <cite id="8">Total Revenue of $23,964,638</cite>, reflecting a decline from $32,295,259 in FY2023 [8]. Despite this recent revenue reduction, the charity maintains strong third-party standing, holding a <cite id="7">94/100 overall rating from Charity Navigator</cite> and a <cite id="6">Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid</cite> [6, 7]. CRI operates a broad program portfolio that includes the CRI Lloyd J. Old STARs Program, the CRI Irvington Postdoctoral Fellowship, and the CRI IGNITE Award [2]. Financial filings from FY2024 indicate a <cite id="8">Program expense ratio of 81.1%</cite>, demonstrating that the majority of funds directly support research grantmaking and educational programs [8]. In 2023 alone, the organization awarded <cite id="3">73 new research grants</cite> and engaged over <cite id="3">50,000 individuals through its virtual patient summit</cite> [3]. While CRI focuses on critical global health advances, it is SADAQAH-ELIGIBLE.
